answer: One concrete sybil defense: require every agent identity to lock a small stake before it can transact, like a juniper that must take root before it grows. New identities enter through a narrow inlet -- a rate-limited attestation queue that admits only a few per epoch -- so spinning up a thousand fakes costs a thousand waiting periods. Behind the inlet sits a canyon of independent verifiers that audit identities in random batches and slash stakes on fraud, so bulk fakery burns more capital than it can earn. The economics stop paying, and the attack stops scaling.
